title: Conventional Commits are enforced in CI
rationale: A machine-readable history drives changelogs and release notes and makes review faster.
hint: Add a PR-title or commit-message check to the CI workflow.

title: CI runs on every pull request
rationale: Nothing reaches main without the same gates that run locally.

title: Dependency updates are automated
rationale: Outdated dependencies are the most common route to known vulnerabilities.

title: SECURITY.md describes a real reporting path
rationale: Reporters need a private channel; template text is a sign nobody looked.

checks.pattern: Use this section to tell people|\[INSERT|your-email@example

hint: Name the contact, the supported versions and the response time.

title: LICENSE is present
rationale: Public code without a licence is not reusable; private code documents its terms.

title: CHANGELOG keeps an Unreleased section
rationale: User-visible changes are written when they happen, not reconstructed at release time.
hint: Keep a changelog; put new entries under [Unreleased].

title: .editorconfig fixes whitespace and line endings
rationale: Editors agree on indentation and newlines, so diffs show only real changes.

title: CODEOWNERS names reviewers
rationale: Every change has an accountable reviewer, also when an agent wrote it.

title: Pull request template asks for the checklist
rationale: The checklist makes the definition of done visible at the moment it matters.

title: Architecture decisions are recorded
rationale: Decisions without a recorded reason are re-litigated or silently reversed.

title: Environment files are git-ignored
rationale: Secrets in history cannot be un-leaked.

title: Third-party dependencies are justified
rationale: Every dependency is attack surface and upgrade work; a register states why it is worth it and what the native alternative was.
hint: Add docs/dependencies.md: name, purpose, native alternative considered, owner.

title: README gives a way in
rationale: A project nobody can start is not a project.

title: A lockfile is committed
rationale: Reproducible installs are the base of supply-chain control.
hint: Commit the lock file; per-project lock files (NuGet packages.lock.json) count anywhere in the repository.

title: Vendor and platform modules are preferred over third-party ones
rationale: First-party and standard-library modules are maintained with the platform, audited more often and carry no extra supply chain.
hint: Before adding a dependency, check the platform first and note the result in the PR.
